purpose: Recovery denominators for the FES25_HT_2050 consumer-bill case (task Y13). The method is the 2030 file's (item D1): metered supply = (GB electrical load + electrolyser draw) / GSP-to-meter loss factor; the hydrogen offtake pays nothing. PRE-RUN: the volumes are FES 2025 HT calendar-2050 figures, declared so the file is complete before the solve; scripts/consumer_bill/refresh_recovery_demand.py replaces them with the solved months' own volumes, which the projector requires.

system_demand_mwh.source: PyPSA annual total of the 12 monthly Stage 1 runs the bill reads (FES25_HT_2050_Jan_market .. FES25_HT_2050_Dec_market: resources/market/<month>_wholesale.nc, every Load's p_set summed over the hours, as read_hourly_inputs measures it)
system_demand_mwh.note: As in 2030: every modelled Load's p_set (GB electrical load plus any hydrogen-bus Load). Kept only so the file can be checked against the run.
system_demand_mwh.refreshed: refreshed 2026-11-21 by scripts/consumer_bill/refresh_recovery_demand.py from 12 months: FES25_HT_2050_Jan_market .. FES25_HT_2050_Dec_market

metered_supply_basis.method: Item D1. Metered supply = (GB electrical load + electrolyser electricity draw) / GSP-to-meter loss factor. The model's loads sit at transmission nodes, so their volume is the GSP-level (loss-inclusive) volume the per-MWh GSP-rate charges are levied on; a household's metered 3.1 MWh draws 3.1 x loss factor at the GSP. Dividing a cost by metered supply is therefore the same as charging the GSP rate on the household's loss-uplifted volume (CfD, allocated CCS, remaining CCS, BSUoS, voltage and stability constraints, AAHEDC, LCCC/ESC, LDES), and is exactly how the RO and FiT, levied on metered supply, recover. The Capacity Market divides by the GSP volume because its household factor already carries losses.

gb_electrical_load_mwh.source: PRE-RUN: FES 2025 HT calendar 2050, ED1 system demand excluding electrolysis (615,323.5 GWh: consumer demand 566,294.5 + losses 49,029.5; ED1 rows 9 less 74, 0.75 FY2050 + 0.25 FY2049) plus DACCS electrical demand (17,828.38 GWh, ES1, not in ED1; decision 25)
gb_electrical_load_mwh.mapping_note: The 2030 identity treats the model's nodal loads as GSP-level (loss-inclusive) volumes, so the pre-run load is the loss-inclusive ED1 system figure. FINDING (Y13): plan Y6 scales the 2050 base to the ED1 consumer total (excluding losses); if the solved loads exclude losses, dividing by the loss factor understates metered supply by about 8% and overstates every per-MWh levy. Decision needed before the refresh (Y6 or coordinator).

electrolyser_electricity_draw_mwh.source: PRE-RUN: FES 2025 HT ED1 row 74 (networked electrolysis), calendar 2050 = 0.75 FY2050 + 0.25 FY2049 (88,775 GWh)
electrolyser_electricity_draw_mwh.note: Refreshed from the Stage 1 link schedules of the electrolysis links, as in 2030.

h2_offtake_mwh.source: PRE-RUN: FES 2025 HT WS1 non-power hydrogen demand, calendar 2050 (road 3.93, residential 0.93, commercial 3.96, industrial 30.33, rail 1.11, shipping 22.32, aviation 28.79, transmission losses 0.05 TWh H2; scripts/FES/fes2025_targets.py hydrogen_quantities)
h2_offtake_mwh.note: Excluded from every electricity denominator. Decision 15 makes non-power hydrogen an annual volume, which may not be a Load; the refresh then reads 0 here and the identity still holds.

gsp_chargeable_volume_mwh.note: The paying volume at the GSP, before the loss factor.

gsp_to_meter_loss_factor.source: Ofgem default tariff cap, Annex 2 (wholesale) tab '3c Electricity losses', GB-average transmission-to-meter loss multiplier, delivery-day weighted over the three 2020 cap periods (data/market/ofgem_price_cap/2020_annual/hedged_wholesale_inputs.csv, column loss_multiplier_gb_average); the multiplier the bill's procurement losses line applies, so the bill carries one loss basis (the projector checks they are equal)

cross_check.ofgem_source: Ofgem default tariff cap Annex 4 v1.25 tab 3i (FiT levelisation): total supply 253.97 TWh, SY16 2025/26
cross_check.note: GSP-level chargeable volume (NESO BSUoS, LCCC) over metered supply (Ofgem FiT levelisation) is 1.08-1.09 on recent outturn, consistent with the 1.092 multiplier; the years differ by one, so this is indicative. NESO chargeable volume and ESPENI GB demand agree to 1.0% (the earlier basis for identifying modelled load with the GSP-level volume).

gsp_to_meter_loss_factor.limitation: A 2020 GB-average multiplier held for 2050 (it must equal the procurement losses multiplier). FES HT 2050 losses are 49.03 TWh on 566.29 TWh of consumer demand, a ratio of 1.0866, close to it.

eligible_share_of_supplier_sales.note: The 2024-25 LCCC outturn share (EII exemption 4.35% of gross sales) held for 2050, declared. FES HT 2050 industrial demand excluding electrolysis is 104.5 TWh (ED1 row 79); the exempt share of it is not forecast.

ro_obligation_eligible_supply_mwh.source: Identified with the CfD eligible-supply volume, as in 2030; the RO is closed in 2050 so no line divides by it

domestic_customer_accounts.note: Cross-check and standing-charge context only; never a recovery denominator.

representative_customer_consumption_kwh.source: Scenario selection, matching the external allowance benchmark
representative_customer_consumption_kwh.note: Used only to express the final representative bill. It is never a recovery denominator.

fes2025_mapping.note: How FES 2025 ED1/ES1/WS1 map onto the bill's denominators (task Y13). Calendar 2050 = 0.75 FY2050 + 0.25 FY2049 (Y1's rule).
fes2025_mapping.gb_electrical_load_mwh: ED1 row 9 (system total) - row 74 (networked electrolysis) + ES1 DACCS: consumer demand + losses + DACCS
fes2025_mapping.h2_offtake_mwh: WS1 hydrogen demand less Power Generation (non-power demand)
fes2025_mapping.final_demand_mwh: (load + draw) / 1.0919: about consumer demand + DACCS + electrolysis at the meter
fes2025_mapping.cfd_eligible_supplier_sales_mwh: final demand x the 2024-25 EII share

limitations: Every share is a recent-outturn share applied to a 2030 modelled volume. It is a stated assumption about scheme scope, not a forecast of eligible supply.

Supplier sales are identified with modelled GB electrical load plus electrolyser draw, net of losses. Behind-the-meter self-consumption that never reaches a supplier meter is inside the model's demand and would, if material, raise the per-MWh levy rates above those reported here.
Electrolysers are treated as ordinary levy payers on their full draw (user decision D1); no exemption for hydrogen production is assumed.
PRE-RUN: FES volumes stand in until the refresh; the projector refuses the file until its volumes match the run.
